newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki airport plans further expansion - paper.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki airport plans further expansion - paper.

text.p: Helsinki-Vantaa international airport has tentative plans to invest 350 million markka in a further expansion of its terminal facilities, daily Kauppalehti reported on Wednesday.
The planned project, due for completion in autumn 1999, is the second phase of the expansion which linked the domestic and international terminals last year, Kauppalehti said.

The so-called middle terminal will now be enlarged to facilitate the special passenger service and luggage handling that will be needed under the Schengen treaty to create passport-free travel in Europe, the paper said.
Finland has recently joined the treaty, expected to take force here in 1999 at the earliest or more likely in 2000, the paper said.
Work is tentatively scheduled to begin at the end of April or early May, but a final decision on the expansion is still pending, Kauppalehti quoted an aviation official as saying.
